name: Retail pad / QSR
summary: Ground-up freestanding quick-service restaurant (1,400–3,500 SF) with drive-thru on a 0.6–1.5 acre outparcel. Cost per SF is high because a small building carries a full commercial kitchen MEP load plus a large share of site work (drive-thru stacking lane, parking, utilities), which franchisor data puts at roughly one-third of building+site cost. Data quality is good: seven 2026 franchise disclosure documents (Item 7) publish building and site-work ranges drawn from recent company and franchisee projects; per-SF conversion depends on assumed building size.

typicalSize.method: Building sizes stated in Item 7 notes: Jack in the Box prototypes 1,386–2,440 SF (e5), Popeyes 1,600–3,500 SF (e3), A&W freestanding 2,082–2,176 SF (e7), Taco Bell traditional ~2,500 SF (e13). Mid = 2,500 SF (Taco Bell / upper JIB / mid Popeyes).

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: Building SF per acre of pad. Lot sizes: Popeyes 28,000–38,000 SF of land (e3), A&W 28,000–35,000 SF (e7), Taco Bell ~0.75 ac (e13), Zaxby's 0.72–1.5 ac (e4). 2,500 SF building / 0.8 ac = ~3,100 SF/ac; 2,100 SF on 1.0 ac = ~2,100; 2,100 SF on 28,000 SF = ~3,300; small 1,400–1,600 SF Go-Mobile style on 0.33–0.5 ac = ~4,500.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: Spaces per building SF. Popeyes: 'typically 25-30 spaces on average' (e3) for 1,600–3,500 SF restaurants → 27.5 / 2,500 = 0.011. Low/high = 25 / 3,000 and 30 / 2,000 rounded.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Building + on-site work per building SF. Item 7 building+site per-project ranges (2025 $): Wendy's $1.03–2.20M (e1); Taco Bell $1.0–2.0M (Dallas, e2); Popeyes $0.74–2.40M (e3); Zaxby's $0.79–2.29M (e4); Jack in the Box $0.96–2.08M (e5); Sonic $1.05–1.50M (e6); A&W $0.50–0.87M (e7). Midpoints median ≈ $1.52M; at the 1,900–2,500 SF typical buildings these brands quote that is ~$600–800/SF, but franchisor highs are skewed by CA/NY sites (e1 is 11 of 34 projects in CA). A&W converts to $240–418/SF (2,082–2,176 SF), RSMeans 2019 fast-food building-only $208/SF ex-architect (e8, ≈$270 in 2025 + ~35% site share ≈ $415/SF), a 2025 Texas McDonald's registration $205/SF (e9, registration estimates are usually partial) and a 2025 consultant benchmark $535–555/SF (e10). Mid $575/SF ≈ $1.44M for the 2,500 SF typical building — between the A&W/RSMeans cluster and the franchisor medians. Low $400 = A&W/RSMeans-with-site; high $850 = JIB/Sonic small-building upper ranges. Excludes kitchen equipment, signage and technology (see ffe), franchise fees, land, impact/tap fees.

scope.notes: Contractor price for building shell + interior + MEP (incl. kitchen hood/exhaust, walk-in box shells are usually in equipment package) and on-site work (grading, paving incl. drive-thru lane, on-site utilities, grease interceptor, landscaping). Excludes kitchen equipment, signage, POS/drive-thru technology (ffe), land, soft costs, off-site improvements, impact/tap fees.

qualityTiers.method: Economy ≈ A&W-type budget prototype ($240–418/SF, e7) vs mid → ~0.78 (= low/mid 450/575 rounded down for small-market builds); premium = high-end franchisor ranges (JIB/Sonic, e5/e6) ≈ 1.25; luxury 1.5 = urban/West Coast flagship with custom architecture (not directly sourced).

systemSplit.method: Site (31+32+33) = 0.36 from franchisor site-vs-building splits: JIB on-site $337–825k vs building $626–1,250k → 35–40% (e5); Sonic site $450–700k vs building $600–800k → 43–47% (e6); Zaxby's sitework $150–990k vs building $640k–1.3M (e4); Popeyes $40–800k vs $0.7–1.6M (e3). Site split 31/32/33 ≈ 22/50/28 (paving and drive-thru lane dominate). Building 0.64 allocated with a restaurant elemental pattern (heavy 22/23/26 for kitchen MEP and hood exhaust/make-up air; 09 finishes; 01 general conditions ~8%). Not a published elemental estimate — verify against a bid.

lineItems.name: On-site improvements (grading, paving incl. drive-thru lane, utilities, landscaping)

cost.method: Franchisor Item 7 site-work lines for new freestanding units: JIB $337,000–$825,000 (e5); Sonic $450,000–$700,000 (e6); Zaxby's $150,000–$990,000 (e4, low end is conversions); Popeyes $40,000–$800,000 (e3, low end is pad-ready sites). Mid = median of new-build midpoints (JIB 581k, Sonic 575k, Zaxby's 570k, Popeyes 420k) rounded to $500k.

lineItems.notes: Carve-out shown for transparency; already inside hardCost (~36% of it). Highly site-dependent (pad-ready outparcel vs raw land).

lineItems.name: Kitchen exhaust hood, make-up air and fire suppression

cost.method: e10: hood with ductwork and make-up air 'can exceed $30,000–$50,000 for a full QSR kitchen configuration' plus fire suppression $2,000–$5,000. Mid $50k; high allows two hood lines (fryer + grill).

lineItems.name: Second (dual) drive-thru lane with order point

cost.method: e10 states a drive-thru 'adds $75,000 to $200,000 to total project cost' and 'Adding a drive-thru lane alone can rise to $200,000'. Mid = geometric-ish midpoint $125k. Low-confidence source.

lineItems.notes: Baseline assumes one lane; add for dual-lane prototypes (e.g., e9 McDonald's dual lane).

lineItems.name: Franchisor construction / design services fees

cost.method: Wendy's FDP Fee $35,000 for new construction (e1); Taco Bell First Unit Construction Services $27,250 (e2); Popeyes construction-management review $20,000–$80,000 if non-qualified CM is used (e3).

lineItems.notes: Soft-cost-like brand fee; only for franchised builds. Initial franchise fees ($35k–$50k) are not included here.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Kitchen equipment + furniture + signage + POS/drive-thru technology per building SF. Item 7 per-project: Wendy's $380,165–$650,000 (e12); Taco Bell equipment/signage/decor/POS $400,000–$577,000 (e2); Popeyes FF&E/signage/tech $340,000–$865,000 (e3); JIB FF&E $499,000–$967,000 + IT $45,000–$60,000 (e5); Zaxby's FF&E $445–497k + tech $75–217.5k + signage $23–245k (e4); A&W signs+tech+FF&E $288,130–$433,148 (e7); McDonald's signs/seating/equipment/decor $1.10–1.85M (e11, larger buildings). Median per project ≈ $550k / 2,500 SF = $220/SF; low = A&W $288k / 2,100 SF ≈ $137; high ≈ $950k / 2,500 SF.

pctOfHard.method: A&E + permits relative to building+site cost: Taco Bell permits/A&E/geotech/testing $75–150k on $1.0–2.0M (7.5%, e2); Zaxby's A&E $45–110k + permits $2–150k (e14); JIB A&E $44–216k + environmental $2.5–34k on $0.96–2.08M (5–12%, e15); A&W professional fees/permits $30–84k on $0.50–0.87M (6–10%, e16); Popeyes soft costs $10k–420k incl. legal, brokerage, traffic studies (e3); consultant guide lists 'Soft costs (permits, design, legal, contingency): $120,000–$200,000' on ~$963k–1.17M hard (10–17%, e10). Adding legal, builder's risk, testing, PM and franchisor fees → mid 12%.

softCosts.notes: Type-specific: initial franchise fee $35,000–$50,000 (Zaxby's $35k, Taco Bell $45k, Wendy's TAF $50k, Popeyes/JIB $50k) and franchisor development/CM fees (line item franchise-design-cm-fees). Impact and tap fees excluded by definition; FDDs flag them as highly variable.

design.method: Prototype drawings are site-adapted, so design contingency is modest; 3–8% typical for adapted prototypes (judgment, consistent with common practice).

hard.method: e10 recommends 'a 10–15% contingency on all QSR builds' (total project). Applied to hard cost only with separate design contingency → 5–12%, mid 8%.

soft.method: Permit/utility-fee volatility noted in every FDD footnote; standard 5–10% of soft costs.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Hard $400–850/SF × (1 + 8–18% soft) ≈ $430–1,000/SF; widened to $380 (rural, pad-ready site) and $1,300 (CA/NY, Sonic-type small building with canopies) per the spread of e1–e7. Excludes land and FF&E.

openQuestions: No published elemental (CSI) breakdown for a ground-up QSR was found; systemSplit is derived — a GC bid tab or public RFP for a QSR would firm it up.
Franchisor Item 7 ranges do not state building SF for Wendy's and Taco Bell; per-SF conversion assumes 2,500 SF.
Wendy's sample is CA-heavy (11 of 34 projects) and Taco Bell is Dallas-only; regionalization of these ranges is approximate.
Burger King, Chick-fil-A and Popeyes building-only per-SF costs from actual GMP contracts would help separate building vs site.
